statement: Priya spent $\dfrac{1}{3}$ of the value of a gift card on a video game. She then spent $\dfrac{1}{4}$ of the remaining value on a controller, and after that she spent $\$36$ on a headset. The card now has $\$24$ left on it. What was the original value of the gift card, in dollars?

choices.misconception: I worked out that $60$ dollars was left after the controller and stopped there instead of finding the original value.
I added $\dfrac{1}{3}$ and $\dfrac{1}{4}$ by adding tops and bottoms to get $\dfrac{2}{7}$ of the card spent, so $\dfrac{5}{7}V = 60$ and $V = 84$.
I took both fractions of the original value, so I solved $V - \dfrac{V}{3} - \dfrac{V}{4} - 36 = 24$ and got $144$.

hints: The $\dfrac{1}{4}$ is a fraction of what was left after the game, not of the original card.
Call the original value $V$. Write what is left after each purchase, one step at a time.
After the game $\dfrac{2}{3}V$ is left. After the controller $\dfrac{3}{4} \cdot \dfrac{2}{3}V = \dfrac{1}{2}V$ is left. So $\dfrac{1}{2}V - 36 = 24$.

solutions.reliable: Let $V$ be the original value. After the game, $\dfrac{2}{3}V$ remains. She spends a quarter of that, so $\dfrac{3}{4} \cdot \dfrac{2}{3}V = \dfrac{1}{2}V$ remains. After the headset, $\dfrac{1}{2}V - 36 = 24$, so $\dfrac{1}{2}V = 60$ and $V = 120$. Check: $120 - 40 = 80$, $80 - 20 = 60$, $60 - 36 = 24$.
solutions.elegant: Work backward: before the headset the card held $24 + 36 = 60$ dollars. That was $\dfrac{3}{4}$ of the amount before the controller, so $80$. That was $\dfrac{2}{3}$ of the original, so the original was $120$.
